policy: Four literal formerly pending key options receive exactly named-species, exactly located plant-organ positive records. The two 'central glume' legacy IDs were anatomically misleading and will be relabeled and illustrated as the LOWER GLUME MIDNERVE; a normal spikelet has lower and upper glumes, not a distinct third central glume. User URL values remain backward compatible. Smooth midnerve and rough midnerve are different observed conditions; glabrous (hairless) is NOT the same as smooth (not scabrous). No species is negatively excluded because another species has a different state.

legacy_option_relabels.display_hint: Examine the middle nerve on the FIRST, LOWER glume, not a supposed third central glume; a smooth surface is not a synonym for having no hairs.
legacy_option_relabels.new_anatomical_interpretation: lower glume midnerve smooth or non-scabrous

legacy_option_relabels.display_hint: Examine the middle nerve on the FIRST, LOWER glume for tiny prickles. Do not score pubescence on a lemma or the spikelet stalk.

evidence.source: West Virginia University Extension, The Identification of Certain Native and Naturalized Hay and Pasture Grasses by Their Vegetative Characters, Plate V fig. 2
evidence.note: Exact Lolium perenne plate depicts the leaf blade in transverse section with deeply RIDGED ADAXIAL UPPER surface; rounded or flattened raised ribs, while lower epidermis is smooth and keeled. Raised lamina ribs are distinct from one pale stripe or visible but flat veins.
evidence.organ_scope: transverse section of mature leaf blade upper (adaxial) surface

evidence.source: AusGrass interactive key, exact Setaria italica species description, mature upper fertile floret lemma
evidence.note: Exact species treatment places 'Lemma apex mucronate' in the FERtile lemma description, not upper/lower glume, lower sterile lemma, involucre bristle or seed. This is a very short tip/point (mucro), NOT the long foxtail bristles below the whole spikelet. Some other sources omit an apex state; treat as nonexclusive positive.
evidence.organ_scope: upper fertile-floret lemma apex, tiny terminal mucro; not bristles

evidence.source: Ahmad & Stewart (1958), Grasses of West Pakistan, Part 1–2, exact Setaria italica species entry, printed p.54
evidence.note: Original exact-species description states the LOWER glume is oblong, hyaline and SMOOTH. The renamed option refers to smooth/not roughened surface including the lower glume's median vein. 'Glabrous' in historical code is a LEGACY ID only, not a license to mistake hairlessness for lack of scabrous projections.
evidence.organ_scope: first/lower outer glume surface, specifically along the median vein

evidence.source: MissouriPlants species account by Daniel E. Tenaglia, Poa annua, lower and upper glumes
evidence.note: Exact species treatment explicitly describes both lower and upper glumes as roughened along the MIDNERVE. The renamed Lab option means a scabrous FIRST/LOWER glume midnerve, NOT a nonexistent central third glume; never infer absence in other grasses.
